# Query repair guidance

Synthetic-only prototype. Nothing here is a clinical-deployment, SMART-authorization, vendor-support or protocol-compatibility claim.

Repair advice never echoes caller input, never names an unreviewed resource type or parameter, and never suggests weakening a constraint: patient confinement, budgets and policy are not negotiable through repairs.

## Repairs by fault code

The repair each fault yields when every name it would mention is reviewed and a larger budget is available (`max_bytes 4096 of 24576`); unreviewed names are left out, and warnings overflow always asks to narrow instead.

`NOT_FOUND` is the uniform answer for absent and foreign records and never carries advice.

## NO_MATCHES

A filtered search that delivered zero authorized matches on an exhausted (terminal) observed chain may carry this warning:

> No matches were delivered for this executed query; this does not establish absence of the clinical concept.

When filter execution is not verified, the fixed sentence "Filter execution is not verified." is appended. The hint is never emitted for unfiltered queries, intermediate pages, unknown exhaustion or pages that delivered matches, and it never describes suppressed entries or upstream totals.

## Observed-code scan (`observed-code-scan-v1`)

For reviewed types whose `code` element is a CodeableConcept (`Observation`, `Condition`, `AllergyIntolerance`, `DiagnosticReport`, `Procedure`), and only when every date pair of the original query uses a reviewed date parameter, the repair suggests a bounded client-side scan: `fhir_search` with `fields: [code]`, `page_size: 100`, at most 3 clinical pages and 4 MCP calls (recipe caps: 20 upstream calls, 45 s, 24,576 B per call, 73,728 B per task). Other types get `discover_search_parameter` through `fhir_capabilities` instead.

| Type | Reviewed date parameters |
| --- | --- |
| `Observation` | `date`, `value-date` |
| `Condition` | `abatement-date`, `onset-date`, `recorded-date` |
| `AllergyIntolerance` | `date`, `last-date`, `onset` |
| `DiagnosticReport` | `date`, `issued` |
| `Procedure` | `date` |

The repair object carries neither the patient context nor the original date window. The gateway still confines every search to the bound patient, but it does not tie a new search to an earlier window: re-applying the original date pairs to the scan and to the follow-up query is the client's obligation.

## Combining observed codes

Build one follow-up `code` value from the returned (system, code) pairs: escape each part (`\`, `,`, `|`) and join the pairs with unescaped commas (OR). Pass that string unchanged as the `params[].value` of `fhir_search`; the gateway URL-encodes it once, so a client must not encode it. A missing system uses the `|code` form, never a bare code, which would match that code in any system. The same code under different systems stays as distinct alternatives. At most 32 pairs are combined and the detailed builder reports truncation; a client must not send a truncated OR list as if it were complete. Splitting an OR value yields at most 32 alternatives and reports truncation: a truncated split keeps the remaining separators inside its last part, which is not a single alternative, so a truncated result must be refused, never consumed as the complete list.
